Otters and Tools

Sea otters are one of very few mammals besides primates known to use tools. They carry a favourite rock in a pouch of loose skin under each forearm and use it to hammer open clams, mussels and snails while floating on their backs at the surface of the sea.

Scientists studying shell middens left by otters along the Californian coast have found evidence that this behaviour is very old, possibly predating the split between sea otter populations thousands of years ago. The rocks show distinctive wear patterns.
